n: God challenges: search Jerusalem’s streets and squares—if you can find even one person who acts justly and seeks truth, I will forgive the city. It recalls Abraham bargaining for Sodom.

f.w: if ye can find a man
the broad places

n: Even when they swear “As the Lord lives,” their oaths are lies. Religious words without honest hearts.

f.w: surely they swear falsely

n: Jeremiah prays: Lord, You look for faithfulness. You struck them, but they felt nothing; You disciplined them, but they refused correction. They made their faces harder than rock.

f.w: they have made their faces harder than a rock
they have refused to receive correction

n: Jeremiah thought: maybe these are just poor, uneducated people who don’t know God’s ways.
So he went to the leaders, who surely knew God’s law—but they too had snapped the yoke and broken the bonds. Rich and poor alike had thrown off the covenant.

f.w: broken the yoke, and burst the bonds

n: So wild beasts will attack: a lion from the forest, a desert wolf, a leopard prowling near their towns—images of the invading armies.

f.w: a wolf of the evenings

n: How can I forgive this? Your children abandoned Me and swore by false gods. When I fed them full, they committed adultery and flocked to prostitutes’ houses. Prosperity led to spiritual and moral decay.

f.w: when I had fed them to the full

n: They were like well-fed stallions, each neighing for his neighbor’s wife—an earthy image of lust out of control.

f.w: fed horses in the morning
neighed after his neighbour's wife

n: Shouldn’t I punish such things? Shouldn’t I avenge Myself on a nation like this?

f.w: visit
f.g: Here means punish or call to account.

n: Enemies are told to go through her vineyard rows and destroy—but not completely. Strip away the branches, for they don’t belong to the Lord.

f.w: make not a full end
battlements
f.g: Probably “branches” of a vine—Israel pictured as a vineyard.

n: Both Israel and Judah have been utterly unfaithful.
They lied about the Lord, saying, “He won’t do anything; no disaster will come; we’ll never see war or famine.” Denying consequences is a classic form of unbelief.

f.w: It is not he
neither shall evil come upon us

n: They say the prophets are just wind with no word from God—so let what they predict happen to them.

f.w: the prophets shall become wind
f.g: A pun: ruach means both wind and spirit.

n: Because they say this, God will make His words in Jeremiah’s mouth a fire and the people wood, and the fire will consume them.

f.w: I will make my words in thy mouth fire

n: God will bring a distant nation—mighty, ancient, speaking a language you don’t understand. This was Babylon.

f.w: a nation whose language thou knowest not

n: Their quivers are like open graves—every arrow brings death—and all their soldiers are warriors.

f.w: an open sepulchre
f.g: An open tomb, ready to swallow the dead.

n: They will devour everything—harvest, food, children, flocks, vines, fig trees—and break down the fortified cities you trusted.

f.w: they shall eat up thine harvest
fenced cities

n: Yet again God promises: even then, I will not make a complete end of you.

f.w: I will not make a full end with you

n: When people ask why God did this, answer: as you abandoned Me and served foreign gods in your own land, so you’ll serve foreigners in a land not yours. The punishment matches the sin.

f.w: so shall ye serve strangers in a land that is not yours

n: Announce this to all of Jacob and Judah.
Listen, foolish people who have eyes but don’t see and ears but don’t hear. Spiritual blindness is willful.

f.w: which have eyes, and see not

n: Don’t you fear Me? I set the sand as a permanent boundary for the sea; waves pound and roar, but can’t cross it. Even the sea obeys God—but His people don’t.

f.w: placed the sand for the bound of the sea

n: But this people has a stubborn, rebellious heart; they have turned away and gone.

f.w: a revolting and a rebellious heart

n: They never say, “Let’s fear the Lord, who gives the autumn and spring rains and guarantees our harvest weeks.” They take blessings for granted.

f.w: the former and the latter
f.g: The early (autumn) and late (spring) rains essential for crops in Israel.

f.w: the appointed weeks of the harvest
f.g: The seven weeks between Passover and Pentecost (Shavuot).

n: Your sins have turned these blessings away and kept good things from you.

f.w: your sins have withholden good things from you

n: Wicked men lurk among God’s people like hunters setting traps—but they catch people, not birds.

f.w: they catch men

n: Like a cage stuffed with birds, their houses are full of things gained by fraud. That’s how they became powerful and rich.

f.w: As a cage is full of birds
f.g: A fowler’s basket packed with trapped birds.

n: They’re fat and sleek, and their evil has no limits. They don’t defend orphans or the poor in court—yet they prosper. God sees injustice toward the vulnerable as a grave sin.

f.w: the cause of the fatherless
They are waxen fat

n: God repeats His question from verse 9: shouldn’t I punish these things?

f.w: Shall I not visit for these things?

n: Something shocking and horrible has happened in the land.
Prophets lie, priests rule by their own authority—and My people love it that way! But what will you do when the end comes? People often prefer leaders who tell them what they want to hear.

f.w: my people love to have it so
bear rule by their means
f.g: Rule at their own direction, or hand in hand with the false prophets.
